transcript.content: This afternoon on the request hour. Ricky, you've got something to tell us!
In your role as head of speech-
You said you were gonna speak.

Oh, no, no. I've just got, er, a fax through about a new club. It's- it's a club I'd, um, I've already heard about. It's called the Chill Club, and it's, um, upstairs, um, at the King's Head. And it's sort of really laid back, and you go in and sit on scatter cushions and be hippy and, and chill out and drink till one and stuff. And, er, they have, like, little acoustic sessions. And, um, that's, er, this Saturday. Saturday the thirty-first.
I think it's every other- I think it's every other Saturday at the King's Head in Fulham.

And, er, um, I've heard good things about it, and it was sold out last week, so they said get there early. Doors are, um, eight thirty, and a bar till, er, one. No entrance after eleven p.m. And, er, it- it's a fiver.

And it's meant to be really cool. A sit-down sort of, you know, trip-hoppy, folky, Portishead-y, jangly sort of stuff. Right up your street, Sturgess. Not Ben's, though. He likes clubbing, doesn't he? Late clubs with, like, loud music and-
Yeah, he gets- goes to bed-
Balti didn't come out of Birmingham.
Yeah, and talking about that, I mean, I stood no one has phoned to confirm or deny the Bolte of Birmingham thing.
I heard the dish. Well, not the actual dish, not the pot, not the lump of clay, but the stuff in it, the particular blend of herbs and spices that we now know as balti...
Maybe he's right. Hold on, no, because it's not the blend of spices. It is the fact that it's called Bolte because you eat it out of the pot. And that I think he's right.

Oh God, I'm backtracking. But thinking about it, yeah, it's not the ingredients. It's the important thing is that it's cooked in that. And of course they didn't invent that there. They... I think he's right, Sturgess.
Slade, I'll get lost. Slade. And if we're counting Led Zeppelin, if we're counting that if we're counting Led Zeppelin, obviously Led Zeppelin.
Oh, no. No, no! Come on!
No, no, you're wrong. Yeah, You're having a mental aberration, if you think.
Go on, give me an example.
Well, there's a fantastic story. Just the ludicrous... ludicrousness. Is that right? Is that a word?

That’ll do, yeah, yeah. Tony Iommi was asked, when they hit big in America, what it was like for Black Sabbath. And he said, “Oh, it was mad. We went back to the hotel and there was, like, ten Satanists sitting outside our hotel room, all dressed in black with black candles.”
So he blew the candles out and sung happy birthday to them.
But, but Led Zeppelin said, “Been a long time since I rock and rolled!” And I think that sums it up.
Yeah, I'm squeezing my little lemon. I'm putting my little, er, cocktail chipolata on the table between two pickled onions and seeing if that fat bridesmaid'll...
And the juice is running down your leg.
Yeah, and the juice is running down my leg. Indeed. Well, we've embarrassed ourselves.
I think in a way, we might have embarrassed XFM.

XFM 104.9. It's just gone quarter past three on a Wednesday afternoon. It's the Request Hour. It's your choice of music. I think we'll have some more music now. This is for Gary O'Donnell, who says chocolate is the best thing to come out of Birmingham. I can't say the brand name 'cause then apparently I'm advertising.
That's not like you to advertise, is it, Sturge?
Sturge, I wouldn't say you advertise. I wouldn't say 'at.
No, no. I mean, you don't want to be pampered.
The limit. The sky is the limit. You know.
Exactly. It's like you've won the lottery.
It's the dry-wife week that I like.
Public Enemy, Anthrax, “Bring the Noise”. That's for, er, Gary O'Donnell this afternoon on the Request Hour. It's XFM 104.9.
It's just gone 20 past 3. Are we going to give away your prize that you bought in specially?
Yeah, we have a winner. Mark Adams from Harrow. With his undercracker explanation.
It is the same one that dropped off Duffo.
He's won it. He'll be able to... Gary's voice check challenge. How good are you at imitating comedian Michael Barrymore? Try this famous catchphrase. All right.
You'll be able to do that.
You'll be able to impress your friends and family.
Where is he? Where, where's Barrymore?
Well, he's at the back. Are you, are you all right at the back?
[Ricky taps and clears his throat to imitate a faulty microphone.]
Here you are. My name is Michael Caine.
Hey, it's like he's in the studio.
Actually, it is nice to see you, Claire. To see you, um, nice.
He didn't just, he didn't... Why do I keep taking off the pop shield?
I know, 'cause I can hit it and be Norman Collier.
I believe if they, if they were gonna rename this book they'd call it the Bible Two.
Mark Adams didn’t just, like, wasn’t grateful for win— He claimed it. He said, “Yes, I, I, I claim that book.”
Quite rightly, he is the winner.
Actually, because we'd forgotten about it, actually, I'd say, so thanks for reminding us.
Have we got his address, have we?
Yeah, fine. Marvellous. I've completely lost my train of thought now.
What am I gonna do next?
What's the chances of that? Usually you're so slick, you know where you are, you're together. Good links, you can string a sentence together. No, um, it's obviously awful.
Studio and see how good Claire is. We'll leave the studio.
This is going to be pretty good, I imagine.
Okay, I'll see you in a minute, then.
Wednesday afternoons in the capital with Fluke Atom Bomb on the request out this afternoon as requested by Phil. I've got my train of thought back.
Well worth waiting for as well.
Incredibly well it's going incredibly well now you may remember all this week I've been trailing a very special guest that was going to be joining us this afternoon Martin Clunes is going to be here.
Sadly as you've probably noticed he's not he's a very busy man he's got lots of stuff to do.
Yeah, it's all the press for the launch and that Terrence Higgins, um...
Exactly so I mean that's cool with us, and he's going to give us a call on Friday.
But I mean, I've got Matt instead, 'cause, er, he's got big ears.
Yeah, yeah. And you smell of booze as well.
Well, yeah, there is that, but, you know.
Hold on, no, I'm not, well, yeah, smell of booze, but we, we meet, we're not saying Martin Clune smells of booze.
We're taking reference to his character in.
We're not saying he likes a drink. We're not saying he's, like, a nonce. But, you know, he, he might, might like a drink.
I'm not saying he's a lush, you know.
No, no. You know, or a teetotaller.
But you're saying I reek of ale?
It's not my fault. After the, you know, 18th one.
It was balancing it on their backs that didn't go down too well.
I felt terrible the other day, though.
Regular as clockwork. On the hour, his right hand starts going. Then his left hand starts going. Yeah. And if he's got a beer in it, it goes all over the place.
It's a bit messy, doesn't it, Matt?
Since the age of 14, you can't keep his wrist still.
The best thing to come out of Birmingham, so says, um, Steve in Surrey. “Ricky, the best thing to come out of Birmingham is yourself when you leave.”
If you were to go to Birmingham tomorrow for the day and then leave Birmingham the next day, you'd be the best thing to come out of Birmingham. That's a compliment.
Excellent, that's nice. What, even better than Pig from Pipkins? Presumably.
The best, it says the best, that's it.
I don't think you're ever gonna leave Birmingham if you go there again after saying that about the people who live there.
They're getting a lynch squad together at the moment.
'Cause the little radio waves that we do just die. Die after the—
M25, they go, “Oh, and that was Mulder and Scu—”
We are the Tumbleweeds. Carl, Graham, Gas Mask Grimshaw. Oh yeah. Mum, Mum, it's getting hot again!
I am. I am. It's fantastic.
You see, Wednesday afternoons at XFM means it's Matt's day. Matt, have you enjoyed yourself today?
Yeah, wild horse wouldn't drag me away.
No. I think you meant to say wild horses, actually.
I know what I mean. Sturgess,

Thank you. It's for the person who phoned or faxed in last week asking for, er, Frente, and we didn't have it. And you said to me, Ricky, “You can't say you don't have it.” But I honestly didn't have it, but now I have it.
So whoever wanted it, it's for you.
To the country. “I can’t wait for Frente anymore. Let’s shoot off.”
Have you just, you've just had someone on the phone or on the fax saying...
Oh, it's voting for the Sneaker Pimps, if they're from Birmingham. I didn't know if they were or not.
I don't know if sneaker pimps are from Birmingham.
What is this obsession with Sabbaths? I always thought Sabbaths were a bit of, like, a joke rock band.
I can't believe you said that.
Led Zeppelin. Is that, like, the mould of the first rock gods? The greatest, er, British band of—what?
Who have Led Zeppelin gone and influenced? You know what they've influenced? That whole brand of poodle rockers with big hair, like Extreme. That's who they've influenced.
Whereas the Sabs, their influence has been really heavy, great rock bands like Nirvana and things like that.
Sabbath are the best thing to come out of Birmingham, Ricky.
Without any shadow of a doubt.
Okay, well, okay, let's do it up to Thursday. I want proper votes, right, on faxes, all right? Who is the best, the most influential, the best, the best band out of Led Zeppelin and Black Sabbath?
It's like comparing Bobby Davro to Tommy Cooper.
I think it's like comparing, uh, let's see. Um...
With Bernard Butler. Bernard Butler being Led Zeppelin.
Oh, well, it's Bobby Davro's brilliant.
You said tomorrow, we're going to have a debate.
It's like comparing something I don't like very much with something I like a lot more.
Yeah, but you like the Smiths, so you're erring on the side of soft, aren't you? Whereas Sabbath are hard.
Yeah, well, I like the hard stuff as well.
So you like Europe and hate Bernard Butler?
Other way round. Other way round!
You hate, you hate Tommy Cooper, but you love Bobby Davro. How's that work?
They're twisting, they're twisting it, Claire! They... Please vote for me! I'm by myself in the studio! 0171 580 2000.
Led Zeppelin's better than Black Sabbath!
I'm a lot better today, by the way, 'cause I've been ill all week with this cold.
Yeah, the mucus fairy came in the night, did he?
Yeah, it did, actually. It was great. Well, there's a... Anyway, yeah.
There’s this fantastic thing from Bristol University. It was in The Times. “Forget hot toddies. The best remedy for a cold is a cup of coffee, according to psychologists at Bristol University.”

The drink largely eliminated the effects of having a cold. They reported after experiments with 100 volunteers. Trials with vodka had failed to show any beneficial effects on mood or performance. Were these trials by vodka, by chance, done around the Christmas party period?
Yeah, they've got to make it look good. Oh, and the control can be, um, coffee.
Vodka versus, um, anything. Coffee, yeah. We do our own.

That’s what that Gold Blend couple was always... They never come to the door going, snot dribbling down, “I’ve just come for some...” Ugh, Jesus, love. Wipe your nose, you filthy... Oh, Jesus. ’Cause it obviously, er, you know, um...
You've been drinking vodka, haven't you? Not the coffee.
Yeah, yeah. Oh no. Oh, you're pissed and you've got snot running down your mouth. Oh, and I, I fancied a good... cup of... um...
Sabbath is like Reef and Led Zep is like the Foo Fighters.
01715802000. Who's the more influential British band? Sabbath or Zepp? Come on, it's obvious. The answer's Led Zeppelin.
I seem to have run out of coffee. Come... come in, I've got some... Oh, sorry.
I've been drinking vodka all day.
The snot's not getting any better.
It's sort of a Led Zeppelin versus Sabbath type quiz.
It's just not a quiz, is it?
Yeah, no. Well, it is really, 'cause there is a right answer. There is obviously a right answer.
No, no, no. Objective speaking, there must be a right answer.
Of which has been, you know, who has been more influential. We could, we could trace it back. Of course we're not the people who do it.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. Well, no, I'm, I'm forgetting the Midlands now.
Oh, really? We're forgetting the Midlands now.
Just, just, er, you know, out of those two. Doesn't matter where they came from.
Who, who is a more influential band on the world rock scene? Sabbath or Zeppelin?
Zeppelin. Ah, Keenan's two to one. At least it's two to one. Right, I'll get rid of him now and we'll be evens, and then it'll be on a vote.
0171 580 2000. We've got ten more minutes till Ian Camfield.
We're just going to get him.
Anyway, Matt, that's a bit of small talk here.
So you've enjoyed yourself today, have you?
He's having an operation. Oh, he's here.
He hasn't been listening. Right. Right. Have you heard what we've just been doing?
I'm gonna ask you. Don't know what, what we think, or who thinks—just answer the question, right?
...who is the most influential band on the world rock scene...
Don't, don't give him any clues.
Who, in your opinion, is the most influential band, or the better band for you, and who influenced more people, out of Led Zeppelin and Black Sabbath?
In what, on what scene? The rock scene? The overall rock scene?
Most influential, you know, in, um, you know, rock and pop.
The best band. It's gotta be Led Zeppelin.

Because, because Led Zeppelin were Led Zeppelin. When they weren't, they folded up. Black Sabbath, great albums with Ozzy Osbourne. Twenty years after that, I'm afraid they went crap. You didn't stipulate the Black—the Ozzy Osbourne period.
You said if we ask Camfield, that'd be definitive. You said it, you laid it on the line. We didn't give any clues. Camfield said Led Zeppelin, that's it. I'm happy with that. Play a record.
Don't even talk to the listeners, Sturgess.
David Keenan took all these, right? Um, uh, Led Zeppelin got every vote except one. Every single person was for Led Zeppelin except one. And that wasn't a Black Sabbath. That was for Dave Keenan.
Out of those two, he said, I'll vote Dave Keenan. Give him his own show. So Zeppelin got all the votes. Sabbath got none. Dave Keenan got more than Black Sabbath. Thank you. It's official.
For the discerning punter, of course, Black Sabbath will always be there. But for people that just say, you know...
For people who haven't got phones.
People who can’t use the phone. “I want to phone, I want to... but I can’t use the phone.” No. Of course, people who can use modern technology, it’s Led Zeppelin.
Excuse me a minute. Who did you say, Sturgess?
Well, I was going for Sabbath.
Right, Sabbath. And did you do the Friday Rock Show on Radio 1?
Well, well, yeah, and so do I!
I think I do. I think I laid my case before you and I rested it there and it was blounding.
That is, er, practically it from us today. Ricky's stormed out of the studio. Keenan stormed with him to answer the phone.
You can come back in again, Ricky. I'm just—this is my goodbye link.
Oh, that's fantastic. Genius. Well done.
And well done to Led Zeppelin for being voted the greatest band, er, most influential band out of them and Black Sabbath.
We, tomorrow, Ricky, it's a shame Matt can't be with us, but tomorrow we are going to have, like a Gary Crowley Battle of the Bands type thing, I think. Like a bit of a demo clash.
Why? Why dig your hole deeper?
Because I want to take this a bit further.
I know, I know, I know, I know.
Thank you. Thank you for listening. Thank you for being discerning, intelligent people. Keep the faxes coming, um, to Ricky Gervais, and Claire and Matt and Dave. They like Black Sabbath.
It's been a pleasure, Matt, having you on the show this afternoon.
Can I say something before I go?
Well, I’m just gonna say, I’m gonna play Mazzy Star into, er, Ian Camfield. “Fade Into You”. And this is for Melinda.
Who wants to hear it, so that's what I'm going to be playing. But I just want to say, Matt, thank you.
That's alright. Can I say something?
Can I just say to Vanessa, food's not love.
We're gonna recreate it. The whole, the tension, the smells, the sights, the sounds, the excitement.
The hot dogs. Most definitely the, the hot dogs.

Yeah, yeah. Um, Matt didn’t know this, but I’m a bit of a Subbuteo buff myself. He comes in here all hard with his sheepskin on, right, with his little team under his arm and his roller, and I go, “I play Subbuteo.” I said, “I do, yeah.”
So, er, well, the gauntlet was laid down.
It was, yeah we've got uh chili against england, but unfortunately I haven't got I haven't got chili so I brought in morocco.
Colombia, yeah so if any of the defenders mess up, I can always shoot one of them.
And that's gonna be live. It's ten minutes each way at twenty to three in the XFM lounge.
We are actually doing a proper football match.
Subbuteo football match on XFM this afternoon. Kick-off at twenty to three, so it's ten minutes each way.
Little boy Fraser's gonna be the referee,
'cause he's the only one that can fit on the pitch and run round.
Without disturbing any of the players.
Of course. It's a work of genius.
And, er, I've, I've picked my team.
Yeah. England, the one I'm in.

No, I've got this, er- look at him! Look at it- look at his face! Gascoigne here. He's so pleased. Look at him there. He's only an inch high, but look at him. I've got Gascoigne, Incey, Batty, um, Seaman there. Do you know what I've got there? It's all over Nigel Martyn, who's in goal.
And, er... I'm gonna put Le Saux there. Um, but it's not mine, Matt brought it in, you filthy... Um, so... anyway, we're gonna-
Apparently, for goalkeepers' choice, though, most women prefer Flowers to Seaman.
Well, so, er, we're gonna- I'm gonna go and, um, check out the pitch, warm up, and, er, Matt-
And where are we doing it? In the Xfm lounge?
Matt's another pint. Um, yeah. Yeah, and we're- a live link with referee and everything. It's gonna be amazing, Claire.
It's- this is radio. This is what radio's meant to be like.
-playing Subbuteo and doing Seaman puns. That is exactly what radio's meant to be.

Okay, let's cross over live now to the living room just down the corner. Let's, er- round the corner, down the corridor. You know what I'm trying to say. The crowds are there. Ricky and Matt are there. Are we ready-
I, I've won the kick-off, Claire, and, er, um, I'm starting off, er-
Oh, listen to the crowd! It's, it's off. We're away. There goes-
It's a beautiful thing. He's moved down the pitch.
It's Chile now! Chile on the break!
England—oh, the, the crowd don't like that much. And, er, he's right up there. There he is.
Barry Spinnaker there and little Tommy Tomkinson.
Oh, there he is. Oh, but they've given it away.
It's a, it's number, it's the number eleven there and he's, he's running—oh, the...
It's a goal kick. There's little boy Fraser there on his horn. Right. On his way to the...
No, we'll be back in a minute.
We can have a penalty shootout, though.
I nearly sprained myself. There. And I had to stop in mid-swing.
We will be back at the XFM living room.
Mum, I don't want any tea. I'm busy!
You're very good with your fingers.
The score, England versus Chile, is nil-nil.
It's time to go back to the XFM Living Room.
For the second half of the match this afternoon, let's see how it's looking.
Well, er, Claire, England are down to ten men. I had to pull one of my players off at half-time.
That's very kind of you. My boys only get oranges.

I used to do that to mine, but they wouldn't put the tights on and have the bag over their head. But here we go, here we go, and it's—oh, look at that lovely ball there. A Hoddle-type ball into nowhere in particular.
Oh, it's Chile again. They've turned round. They're in my—oh, they've fouled his own player. They've missed it completely. England move up there. And it's a dirty foul. It's a dirty foul.
Quite a dangerous area. He's moving two. He's not...
Oh, here we go. I've never been in such close proximity to you, Ricky.
England in possession again. Oh, look at this move here.
It's like you have to show 'em.

Oh, they're, they're keeping it. They're playing with the ball now. Oh! It's a foul, it's a foul! They're gonna take it quickly. It's there. Oh, it's a bit dangerous. England in the fifteen yards—oh! So close.
Still England's there. It's in a dangerous position.
That is the end of the match then. So, I guess, what, extra time? Penalty shootout?

So, as we recreate the England-Chile match tonight, this afternoon in fact, here live on XFM, down there in the living room we have Ricky and Matt. Ricky representing England on the Subbuteo table. Matt is doing the business for Chile, although he hasn't got any Chile team members.
He's using the Colombia ones. But don't you worry about that. We cross over live now, back to the XFM living room.
The Tannoy's on. Um... Well, England are going to take the first penalty. It's just the best of three. And his goalkeeper keeps jumping up and kicking it with his back.
Yeah. That's ridiculous. Well, can I just, like, say as well, I feel slightly stupid, 'cause we could be in the studio pretending to play this, but we are two grown men...
Sprawled out. My knees are killing me. We've got the whole thing out. It, it took us about an hour to tape it down.
I'm in trouble with me mum because I'm missing me tea.
Yeah. Yeah. Right, here we go.
Okay, let's just very quickly— so the score is nil-nil. This is a penalty shootout. Off you go.
Oh, I can't believe it. Okay.
Chile have to score this to stay in.
They can't— that's it! They can't, they can't win!
Just like to say thanks to everyone that, um, that had faith in me. I, I, I— you know, I knew I could do it. There was a lot of criticism, but thanks! Thanks! We've done it! We've done it!

And as we say goodbye to the XFM living room, there's Chumbawamba with tub-thumping playing over the tannoy. Oh, the boys will be back in the studio for a bit of a post match analysis. Joined by ricky Gervais and matt unbound team captains, ricky Gervais england and that's Unbound Chile, although it was Colombia, but it's only because...

The really embarrassing thing is, not only that we actually went through with it, but that we didn't care whether it was on the radio or not. We were having a brilliant time. In my heart I just wanted to win so badly, Claire.
I just wanted to win so badly. Oh God, and when I put that goal past him, he just— oh God, it was just amazing.
Yeah, you looked like a happy man. And the boy Fraser did well.
He was, he was loving it.
He was jumping up and down.
He ruled it with a rod of iron.
I know, yeah. I know, yeah. We— well, we'll leave it there.
Do you know what we haven't had time to do this afternoon, Matt?
All those autographs you got from the awards.
You've got— we've got all those autographs and we were gonna give 'em away today. Now, what do you reckon? Shall we do it next week?
No, I'm going to keep them.
No, all right, we'll come up with a competition. That's what—
We'll do it next week. I mean, seriously, Ricky, we have got all these autographs.
That's— that is a lovely prize, quite seriously. You didn't really get Krankie, did you?
I didn't get Krankie, no, no.
At least, at least he said off— off drinking gin.
But once again, thank you for the effort you put in this afternoon for that match.
Oh, it- it was my pleasure.
Um, and the fact that, you know, it's not sad, the fact that you did actually play-
Did you see the second goal, though?
I did see the second goal.
And I also, Ricky, what I-
No, I wanted England to win, so that's it. That's the match.
[Music fades and the recording cuts to the studio.]
Gervais, we've had a fax. There's a guy, he's desperate for our help. I'm not gonna deny it, he's desperate. He's a desperate man, Gervais.
Basically, the situation is this. Uh, he's got a small boat, and he's got to row it across a river.
Well, that might seem straightforward enough.
Okay, but this fella has to take with him, Gervais, a fox, a chicken, and a big bag of seed.
Well, he's, he's got a nightmare problem.
Why? He just put- wait, what? Why? So he puts the seed-
Well, because, no, listen, because the boat is only big enough for him and one of those items at any one time.
It's only- he can get in it,
And any one of those other items.
Any one of those other items.
Fine. Um, he takes the bag of seed over, rows it over, dumps that the other side.
While he's happily rowing across with that bag of seed...
Um, I've got to ask you something here, right? This boat is small, yeah?
It's a small boat, I'm not gonna deny it.
So he can fit any one of those things in, yeah? So am I to assume that the chicken is the same size as the fox is the same size as the bag of seed?
Which is... so it's the same size as the fox, which is the same size as the bag?
Then why is he worried about it being a bloodbath? Surely the chicken can look after itself if it's, it's— weight for weight it's the same as the fox.
No, well, what are you talking about? A chicken, fox? I mean, you know, you put a chicken and a fox, you know, in arm-to-arm combat—
Good reason. The average fox is like two stone.
The average chicken is ten pounds. Yeah. Scale that up. Imagine what a two stone chicken looked like with a nasty beak and talons.
I'm not saying it's not a big chicken. That is a given, all right?

You, you, you pit that chicken against the fox. Maybe that chicken's been taking that fox on all over the place, you know? They could've been on trains together, d'you know what I mean, sharing hotel rooms. The chicken's knackered, all right? All I'm saying is that guy, right, while he's rowing across that bag of seed, he cannot leave that chicken—
Okay, okay, right, okay, right, right, yeah. So, okay, fine. So he's now— chicken and fox, bag of seed, all the same size, all the same weight.
Right, okay. Why couldn't he— why couldn't he just, like— okay, I'm assuming he's rowing, so he's got some give—
Right, with a— so why, why can't he have the bag of seed under his knees, right, and the chicken just sort of like, sort of flapping?
He just can't. There's no— d'you know what I mean? He doesn't— look, the point is, right, this guy's contacted us.
He thinks, do you know what I mean?
All right, all right, okay, shut up. Okay, forget it then, right. So he's got the fox, chicken and that. So, okay then, he takes the fox over, no bloodbath, drops that off, comes back...
Wait, wait, wait a minute. Gervais, embarrassment.
That chicken's gonna eat that bag of seed faster than.
This— hold on. This bag of seed, presumably some sort of, like, hemp material, maybe sacking, woven...
Well, that chicken's huge! Got huge great, you know, claws, talons even.
So it could— it would rip it apart, would it?
So it could open the bag of seed?
But it couldn't contact— it couldn't compete with that fox. Let me just, you know, get that straight.
Okay, so he takes the chicken over.
Dumps that off. No, he can leave the fox with the bag of seed, can't he?
That's not a problem, 'cause, you know, seed and fox. A fox is not interested in seed, Gervais. Don't go nuts.
Brings the fox back, dumps the fox with the seed, yeah?
Wait a minute, wait, so what, hang on, maybe you're onto something here, wait.
He's taken the— he's taken the seed. No, he can't take the seed.
Oh, no, he's taken the fox.
He's left the chicken with the seed.
No, hang on, what, but you said he's taken...
Oh, no, no. He's taken the fox over.
No, he's taken the chicken over.
And left the fox and the seed.
Leaves the chicken there, then he comes back.
